title: Extreme Meta-classification for Large-Scale Zero-Shot Retrieval

problem.claim: Large-scale retrieval must handle novel zero-shot items arriving continuously and rapidly.

gap.claim: Siamese-style encoders lack sufficient capacity for complex retrieval tasks, while extreme classifiers cannot be trained for novel items because of data and latency constraints.

contributions.claim: EMMETT synthesizes classifiers on the fly for novel items using classifiers available for observed items.
IRENE is a simple, effective EMMETT instance designed for large-scale deployments.
The paper develops a theoretical framework for analyzing generalization performance in large-scale zero-shot retrieval.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe EMMETT and IRENE as new.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across a wide range of retrieval tasks, IRENE improved zero-shot retrieval accuracy by up to 15 percentage points in Recall@10 when added to leading encoders.
In an online A/B test for large-scale ad retrieval at a major search engine, IRENE improved ad click-through rate by 4.2%.
Extensive ablation experiments were used to validate the design choices.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets accurate and efficient retrieval with continuously arriving zero-shot items.
Siamese-style systems embed queries and items with a small encoder and retrieve nearby items.
Siamese encoders have insufficient capacity, whereas extreme classifiers face difficulty handling novel items.
EMMETT, IRENE, and a theoretical framework are introduced to bridge the capacity and novel-item constraints.
Experiments, an online A/B test, and ablations report accuracy, click-through-rate, and design-validation results.
